caption: The drawing depicts a white or light beige rectangular textile, possibly a towel or cloth, folded into three horizontal sections. The fabric has a slightly uneven, soft texture and features a fringe along the bottom edge, with individual strands visibly hanging down. Embroidered designs are present, stitched primarily in red and dark green thread. At the top of the textile, there is text reading "1803" and "BALI WEISER" in red, formed in a simple, blocky stitched style. Below the text, on each visible fold, there is a symmetrical, vertically oriented motif resembling a stylized floral or tree form, also stitched in red and green. Each motif consists of geometric shapes arranged to suggest a central stem with branching, decorative offshoots and small cross-like or star-shaped flowers at the ends. The embroidery is centrally positioned on each fold, and the overall arrangement emphasizes the length of the textile, aligning the motifs one above the other. The background is plain, with no additional objects or colors present.
title: Pa. German Embroidered Towel
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
